page: Microsoft Azure L8aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Laosv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and features a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic accelerations like AES and SHA_NI. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, and includes a substantial 5760 GB local NVMe SSD storage array.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff: while small-block cached read bandwidth is average at 607.81 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth is weak, registering at 36.3 GB/sec. Large-block write bandwidth remains average at 28.23 GB/sec. Database operations, evaluated via PassMark and Redis SET operations (11.68 million operations per second), perform in the middle tier. Large-model LLM inference is limited, with medium 7B model prompt processing scoring in the bottom 25%, though small 135M model processing remains average.

Given the high density of local NVMe SSD storage (5760 GB) relative to the 8 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, the L8aos_v4 offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for storage-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. The combination of a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high-capacity local storage makes this server well-suited for relational databases, NoSQL data stores, caching layers, and text processing applications. However, the weak uncached large-block memory read bandwidth and average multi-core scaling suggest it is less optimal for memory-bound high-performance computing or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Microsoft Azure L8aos_v4 is an x86_64 storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores) running at 3.7 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of RAM and a large 5760 GB local NVMe SSD. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, placing in the top 25%, while multi-core and database operations perform in the average tier. A key tradeoff is its memory bandwidth, where cached small-block reads are average but uncached large-block reads are weak. With a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high local storage capacity, this instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for storage-heavy applications. It is best suited for databases, caching layers, and text processing workloads, rather than memory-bound high-performance computing or large-scale LLM inference.
